newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares advance on technical factors.
newsitem.headline: German shares advance on technical factors.

text.p: German shares advanced strongly in bourse trade on Thursday, but dealers said the market was driven predominantly by technical factors rather than by any new data moving the market.
At 0920 GMT, the DAX index was up 24.38 points, or 0.65 percent, at 3,754.65 points, while the June DAX future was up 27 points at 3,753.5 points.

Derivative products drove the market ahead of Friday's "triple-witching", which sees the expiry of DAX index options, DAX futures and stock options and traditionally brings volatility into the market.
"This market is more technical than fundamental at the moment ahead of the triple witching, and it's causing movements right across Europe, not just in Germany," said a Frankfurt trader.
Derivatives buying lifted Volkswagen AG in particular early on, with the share up 33.2 marks at 1,253 marks, the dealer said.
The carmaker was also expected to report figures at its annual general meeting in Hamburg.
Technical factors also drove airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG higher, rising 5.31 percent to 34.30 marks.
Shares in retailer Karstadt fell against the trend by 4.13 percent to 627 marks, after disappointing five month figures.
"There isn't really any news out there -- it's all derivatives-driven. There is a lot of progressive buying coming from the U.S., and demand exceeds supply in this market," the trader said.
